text:
maria (Support): heads up — acme reported a spike in generation latency around 00:12 UTC, p95->p99 jumped to ~500ms and traces show requests routing to ap-south-1 instead of eu-west-1. customer says it started right after a midnight batch. attaching trace id 6f3b2a.
jamal (SRE): can you paste the trace? any 5xxs or auth errors?
maria (Support): no 5xx, just high tail latency. trace snippet:
```
trace 6f3b2a: /v1/generate -> routed-> gateway-ap-south-1 -> backend-dedicated-3
latency: client->gw 30ms, gw->backend 460ms
route-policy: fallback:region-weight-based
```
noah (Customer): seeing this from our end too. our app is pinned to eu-west via `X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1` header normally. we didn't change anything.
sasha (Eng Runtime): @maria thanks. two quick hypotheses: (1) region affinity lost because token TTL expired and our sticky session fallback picked another region, or (2) a peering flap caused route weights to shift and our smart router chose ap-south due to perceived lower cost.
jamal (SRE): checking infra metrics — I see a transient spike in inter-region egress error counts at 00:10 UTC from eu-west -> eu-peer. graph: small blip, then connections recovered. could have triggered fallback.
maria (Support): customer says pattern is repeatable nightly around 00:00-00:20. they suspect a cron job.
sasha (Eng Runtime): can we get the full trace span list? also any KV cache invalidation logs around midnight? sometimes cache eviction removes prefix affinity and requests fall back to routing heuristics.
maria (Support): full trace attached inline: `span[0] gw start] -> span[1] routing decided ap-south-1 (reason: fallback-weighted, error rate eu-peer 0.12) -> span[2] backend connect`
jamal (SRE): running rtrace on 6f3b2a... returns route decision payload: `{"candidate_regions":["eu-west-1","ap-south-1"],"scores":{"eu-west-1":0.48,"ap-south-1":0.52},"reason":"egress-peering-penalty"}`
noah (Customer): is there any short-term mitigation? our SLAs get hit when latency spikes.
sasha (Eng Runtime): short-term: set `X-Redwood-Region` header to `eu-west-1` from client side to force affinity until we fix routing. long-term: we need to prevent midnight peering penalties from overwhelming route score.
jamal (SRE): can also pin via per-tenant routing override for Acme. I'll push a temporary policy.
infra-bot: deploy started: apply-routing-override acme -> eu-west-1 (canary)
maria (Support): applied to 10% of traffic, noah can you confirm if latency improves for canary?
noah (Customer): canary looks good, p99 back to ~120ms for tagged requests. thanks. :thumbsup:
sasha (Eng Runtime): root cause hypothesis: upstream peer maintenance at midnight increased transient error penalty in scoring algorithm, combined with prefix cache churn that removed per-tenant affinity. action items: 1) adjust scoring to dampen brief peering blips; 2) add KV curb prewarm before midnight batch windows; 3) add per-tenant sticky fallback that prefers last-known region.
jamal (SRE): I'll open infra ticket and schedule a short postmortem. ticket INFRA-4789.
maria (Support): customer happy with mitigation but requested us to keep them in the loop. tagging @noah for follow-up.
infra-bot: deploy complete: routing-override canary -> 10% applied
sasha (Eng Runtime): logging follow-up: collect more rtrace outputs around 23:50-00:30 for the last 7 days to see pattern. also check token refresh logs for tenants using ephemeral session tokens — that could explain affinity loss.
maria (Support): noted. closing loop with Acme and will update with PM. :eyes:
